CONTESTED DOCUMENTS AND FPORGERIES. 
By ¥. BREWESTER. 


The volume under review is one of the most lucid 
works that has been published on this much written about 
and still more widely discussed subject. 

The author's chapters on handwriting production and 
development are written in s0 plain a language, avoiding 
as far as possible, the use of technical terms, thas no 
previous knowledge of the subject is required to understand 
it. He also very successfully refrains from committing 
a fault common to most writers on handwriting who generally 
begin with clear and concise information regarding the 
formation of handwriting, following it up to maturity, and 
then suddenly merge into realms of psychoeanalysisa without 
clearly explaining how tc tell genuine writing from a 
spurious one, or giving any tangible clue as to methods of 
proving ite 

Mir. Brewester strictly adheres to the title of his 
book and gives a full but simple explanation of the work 
confronting « handwriting expert in proving forgery, etc. 
in a Court of Law, and in addition puts his reacers in 
possession of knowledge wherewith to prove his assertions. 
Moreover he does not minimize the responsibility of an 
expert and takes the trouble to show that many persons, 
posing as experts, are absolutely unqualified and thus 


greatly jeopardize the value of opinion by a real expert 


when he is called upon to give evidence. 


The chapter dealing with seals and impressions is 
very likely to make many dubious about putting as much 
faith in this form of security as they might have done 


heretofore. 


In the chapter on finger prints as a means of 
identification, the author seems inclined to be rather 
doubtful in upholding the belief that no two finger 
prints of different pversons are ever identical. He does 
admit, however, that failure to find two alike in all the 
millions which have been examined justifies the assumption 
that there are none identical. No finger print expert 
can find fault with this assertion, but in the face of the 
author's definite stater-ent in the first chapter of his 
book that “No two persons ever write precisely alike" the 
question arises as to whether this can be as definitely 
laid down vis a vis the "no two alike" theory regarding 
finger prints being assumed only in the absence of proof 
to tie contrary. The same theory should, therefore, 
hold good in the matter of handwriting as it is not 
impossible that even more finger prints than documents in 
handwriting have been compared for identification purposes. 

The foregoing is only a friendly criticiam at the 
request of the author and, whilst from the point of view 
of a finger print expert there are several little points 
which may be termed slightly inaccurate, tnese do not in 
any way tend to spoil a very interesting and instructive 
chapter on finger prints. 

Mr. Brewester also discusses the subject of placing 
forged finger prints on documents such as promissory 
notes, etc., and although he very discreetly refrains 
from telling his readers how this is actually done, he 
states this type of offence as being fairly common in 
India. The one likely comment in this connection is that, 
if privately taken, finger prints in India with the above 
object in view are no clearer than some of those seen in

The author has, furthermore, rendered great service

The book is concluded with a chapter on document

former is not intended to teach people photography, but

It would be unfair to close the review without

excellent illustrations throughout the book, which are

《争议文件与伪造品》。
F. BREWSTER 著。

这本受评著作是关于这一被大量撰写且讨论更为广泛的主题所出版的最清晰明了的作品之一。

作者关于笔迹形成与发展的章节语言平实，尽可能避免使用专业术语，因此无需具备该主题的先前知识即可理解。他还非常成功地避免了一个大多数笔迹作家常犯的错误，即通常先提供关于笔迹形成直至成熟期的清晰简明的信息，然后突然转入精神分析领域，却没有清楚地解释如何区分真迹与赝品，也没有提供任何关于证明方法的具体线索。

Brewster 先生严格遵循其书名，充分而简单地解释了笔迹专家在法庭上证明伪造等行为时所面临的工作，此外还使读者掌握用以证实其论断的知识。而且，他并未低估专家的责任，且不辞辛劳地指出，许多自称专家的人完全不具备资格，从而在真正被传唤作证的专家提供意见时，极大地损害了其意见的价值。

关于印章和印鉴的章节很可能会让许多人不再像以前那样对这种安全形式抱有如此多的信任。

在关于指纹作为识别手段的章节中，作者似乎倾向于对“不同个人的两个指纹绝不会相同”这一信念持相当怀疑的态度。然而，他确实承认，在已检查的数百万份指纹中未能找到两个相同的指纹，这一事实证明了假设不存在相同指纹是合理的。任何指纹专家都无法对这一断言提出异议，但鉴于作者在本书第一章中明确陈述“没有两个人的笔迹完全相同”，这就引出了一个问题：既然关于指纹“没有两个相同”的理论仅是在缺乏反证的情况下被假定的，那么这一理论是否也能同样明确地适用于笔迹问题？因此，同样的理论也应适用于笔迹事项，因为为了识别目的而比较的指纹数量甚至可能多于笔迹文件数量，这并非不可能。

上述内容仅是应作者要求提出的友好批评，虽然从指纹专家的角度来看，有几个小点可以称为稍不准确，但这丝毫不会损害这一关于指纹的非常有趣且富有启发性的章节。

Brewester 先生还讨论了在票据等文件上放置伪造指纹的问题，尽管他非常谨慎地未告诉读者这实际上是如何操作的，但他指出此类犯罪在印度相当普遍。对此可能有的评论是，如果在印度出于上述目的私下采集的指纹并不比在中国出于同样目的采集的一些指纹更清晰，那么诸如之类的伪造必要性就应当消除，因为可以肯定，没有任何专家能够通过这类指纹识别任何人。

The chapter on typewriting identification upholds
the high standard obtaining in the preceding ones. Both
the clearness with which readers are told how to identify
machines on which specific documents have been written
and the points of identification to be looked for leave
nothing more to be desired.

The author has, furthermore, rendered great service
to students of handwriting by his chapter on Courts and
their procedure, examination, cross-examination and re-
examination and all who are likely to appear in Courts
either as witnesses or Counsel should derive much useful
information from their perusal.

The book is concluded with a chapter on document
photography and another on the English script. The
former is not intended to teach people photography, but
only to give advice to photographers in dealing with
disputed documents, whilst the latter is extremely useful
to expert students and interesting to lay readers. The
following statement, for example, may give many a reader
much food for thought:- "It has been calculated that
the twenty six small letters in the alphabet can be written
in 2,016,557,305,632,323,277,920,000 different ways",
and the reviewer for one is not prepared to dispute the
authenticity of this number.

It would be unfair to close the review without
complimenting the author and his photographer on the
excellent illustrations throughout the book, which are
both helpful and numerous.

关于打字机识别的章节保持了前几章的高水准。无论是向读者清晰说明如何识别书写特定文件的机器，还是指出需要留意的识别要点，都令人满意，无可挑剔。

此外，作者通过其关于法庭及其程序、讯问、交叉讯问和再讯问的章节，为笔迹研究者提供了极大的帮助，所有可能以证人或律师身份出庭的人都将从阅读中获得许多有用信息。

本书以关于文件摄影的一章和关于英文字体的一章作为结尾。前者并非旨在教授人们摄影技术，而仅是就处理争议文件向摄影师提供建议，而后者对专家学生极为有用，对普通读者也颇有趣味。例如，以下陈述可能会给许多读者带来深思：“据计算，字母表中的二十六个小写字母可以用 2,016,557,305,632,323,277,920,000 种不同的方式书写”，而书评人本人并不准备质疑这一数字的真实性。

如果不称赞作者及其摄影师在全书中提供的出色插图，结束这篇书评是不公平的，这些插图既有益又丰富。
